expected_text_segments: Gold before the jobs report: beyond the Fed's target range
Treasury's nominal 10-year yield fell 5 basis points on November 4; its real yield fell 1. The next question for gold is how real yields respond to the November 6 jobs report.

A lower Treasury yield is an incomplete guide to gold. On November 4, Treasury's nominal 10-year par yield was 4.90%, down from 4.95% on November 3. Its real 10-year yield was 2.64%, down from 2.65% on the same dates.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics schedules the October Employment Situation for November 6 at 8:30 a.m. EST. Capital Chronicle's view is that the useful follow-up for gold is whether the inflation-adjusted yield moves lower. The jobs outcome is still ahead.

## Two yields, two questions

The nominal Treasury series quotes a yield without an adjustment for inflation; the real series is its inflation-adjusted counterpart. Lower real Treasury yields would reduce one cost of holding gold: the inflation-adjusted return available from a competing asset. That is the economic channel being watched, rather than a measurement of gold's reaction.

The [Federal Reserve's October 28 statement](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20261028a.htm) recorded a target range for the federal funds rate of 3.75%-4.00%. That dated policy range anchors the discussion, but it is a different measure from the 10-year bond yields relevant to this watch.

## The latest fall was mostly nominal

Calculated from Treasury's November 3 and 4 observations, the nominal decline was 5 basis points and the real decline was 1 basis point. One basis point is 0.01 percentage point. The daily comparison therefore shows much less easing in the real measure. These yield observations do not establish how gold traded.

## What to watch after the jobs report

After the release, a sustained fall in the real 10-year yield would strengthen this particular case for gold. A fall in the nominal yield with the real yield little changed would offer less support through the same channel. A sustained real-yield rise after the jobs report would weaken this particular support for gold.

## What would weaken the argument

Currency moves or demand for safety could outweigh the real-yield channel. That would make a simple bond-yield explanation inadequate. A gold rise alongside rising real yields, or a gold decline alongside falling real yields, would challenge a one-channel reading. The checkpoint is the observed real-yield response after the release, then whether gold moves consistently with that mechanism.

Analysis, not financial advice. Readers decide whether to trade. Capital Chronicle may hold positions in the markets it covers.
